target: Syrthiodd e i gysgu yn ystod y ffilm.
english: He fell asleep during the film.
tip: syrthio i gysgu is the set phrase for 'fall asleep', literally 'fall to sleep': Syrthiodd e i gysgu.

target: Byddwn ni'n cael swper am saith o'r gloch.
english: We will have dinner at seven o'clock.
tip: Byddwn ni = we will (future). Swap ni for i and Byddwn i means 'I would' (conditional). The pronoun sets the meaning.

target: Clywodd Heledd y plant yn chwerthin yn yr ysgol.
english: Heledd heard the children laughing at school.
tip: yn plus a verbnoun renders '-ing' after verbs of perception: y plant yn chwerthin = the children laughing.

target: Roedd tri o blant yn chwarae yn y parc.
english: There were three children playing in the park.
tip: The linking word o (of) softens the next consonant: plant (children) becomes o blant here.

target: Mae hi wedi ysgrifennu dau lyfr am hanes Cymru.
english: She has written two books about Welsh history.
tip: wedi replaces yn to make the perfect 'have done': Mae hi wedi ysgrifennu (she has written).

target: Agorodd hi'r ffenest i adael awyr iach i mewn.
english: She opened the window to let fresh air in.
tip: i before a verb shows purpose: i adael = in order to let. Agorodd hi'r ffenest i adael awyr = opened it to let air.

target: Mae'r Gymraeg yn un o'r ieithoedd hynaf yn Ewrop.
english: Welsh is one of the oldest languages in Europe.
tip: Superlatives end in -af: hen (old) becomes hynaf (oldest) in yr ieithoedd hynaf (the oldest languages).

target: Bydd y trên yn gadael am hanner awr wedi tri.
english: The train will leave at half past three.
tip: Welsh says half past as hanner awr wedi tri, literally 'half an hour past three'. Here wedi means 'past'.

target: Roeddwn i fod i gwrdd â hi am dri o'r gloch.
english: I was supposed to meet her at three o'clock.
tip: Roeddwn i fod i means I was supposed to; i fod i marks an arranged or expected action.

target: Ym mhoced fy nghôt.
english: In my coat pocket.
tip: fy (my) triggers nasal mutation: côt becomes nghôt. So fy nghôt means my coat.

target: Yr ail o Fehefin.
english: The second of June.
tip: o (of) triggers soft mutation: Mehefin becomes Fehefin. The month softens after o in dates.

target: Prynais i ddwy gôt.
english: I bought two coats.
tip: The object of an inflected verb soft-mutates its first word: dwy becomes ddwy in Prynais i ddwy gôt.

target: Derbyniodd e'r cynnig swydd.
english: He accepted the job offer.
tip: Welsh past tense keeps Verb-Subject-Object order: Derbyniodd e'r cynnig = he accepted the offer, verb first.

target: Bore da, shw' mae?
english: Good morning, how are things?
tip: shw' mae is the south Wales greeting for how are you. The north says sut mae instead.

target: Difrodоdd y storm y to.
english: The storm damaged the roof.
tip: Welsh puts the verb first: the sentence opens with the verb, then y storm, then y to (the roof).

target: Mae ei dad yn ffermwr.
english: His father is a farmer.
tip: ei (his) triggers soft mutation: tad becomes dad. So ei dad means his father.

target: Mae'r canhwyllbren yn dal pum cannwyll.
english: The candelabra holds five candles.
tip: After a number the noun stays singular: pum cannwyll is literally five candle, not candles.

target: Rhedodd e bum milltir cyn brecwast.
english: He ran five miles before breakfast.
tip: A noun stays singular after a number: bum milltir = five miles, not a plural. pump shortens to bum here.

target: Mae'r ffaith bod e yma'n bwysig.
english: The fact that he's here is important.
tip: bod carries that in a fact clause: y ffaith bod e yma means the fact that he is here.

target: Mae dwy bont dros yr afon.
english: There are two bridges over the river.
tip: dwy is the feminine two and softens the noun: pont becomes bont. dwy bont means two bridges.

target: Y gardd sy tu ôl i'r tŷ.
english: It is the garden that is behind the house.
tip: sy is the relative verb form for which is or that is: y gardd sy tu ôl means the garden that is behind.

target: Cwynodd hi fod y gwasanaeth yn wael.
english: She complained the service was poor.
tip: Report 'that' with a bod form: Cwynodd hi fod y gwasanaeth yn wael = she complained that the service was poor.

target: Mae ei fam-gu yn naw deg oed.
english: His grandmother is ninety years old.
tip: Age uses yn plus oed: naw deg oed means ninety years old, literally ninety of age.

target: Dw i'n teimlo'n hapus heddiw, diolch byth.
english: I feel happy today, thank goodness.
tip: diolch byth is a set phrase for thank goodness, literally thanks ever.

target: Roedd pedwar tymor, pob un yn hardd.
english: There were four seasons, each beautiful.
tip: Welsh 4 changes by gender: pedwar with masculine nouns like tymor, pedair with feminine ones.

target: Dydyn ni ddim angen unrhyw help, diolch.
english: We don't need any help, thank you.
tip: Negatives use ddim after the verb: Dydyn ni ddim means we do not.

target: Mae pob taith yn dechrau gydag un cam.
english: Every journey begins with one step.
tip: gyda becomes gydag before a vowel: gydag un cam means with one step.

target: Mae angen batri newydd ar ei gar e.
english: His car needs a new battery.
tip: Welsh has no verb for need: mae angen X ar Y means Y needs X. angen batri ... ar ei gar is his car needs a battery.

target: Mae'r cyfarfod yn dechrau am chwarter wedi dau.
english: The meeting starts at quarter past two.
tip: wedi means past when telling time: chwarter wedi dau is quarter past two.

target: Mae'r plant wrth eu bodd yn ymweld â'u nain.
english: The children are delighted to visit their grandmother.
tip: wrth eu bodd is an idiom for delighted, literally at their pleasure.
